why: We need every OR value over strictly increasing subsequences. That is LIS-style DP where the state is not a length but the set of reachable ORs: ending[v] = the ORs of increasing subsequences ending in value v, built from ORs ending in smaller values. Values are < 1024, so ORs fit in 10 bits and each set is a 1024-bit mask.
hints: Like LIS, process elements left to right. An element x can extend any increasing subsequence whose last value is < x.
The OR result is < 1024, so represent 'reachable ORs' for each last value as a bitmask over 0..1023. x extends every OR o reachable with last value < x, giving o | x.

Use a Fenwick tree (prefix-OR over values) of masks to get 'all ORs with last < x', and only expand ORs not already seen for x (each (value, OR) pair is processed once). Total about O(1024 * 1024 + n log 1024). Add 0 for the empty subsequence.
pitfalls: The empty subsequence counts: 0 is always in the answer.
Strictly increasing: equal values cannot extend each other ([5,5] is not allowed).
Re-expanding the same OR many times is O(n * 1024) per element, too slow. Track what was already fed into each value.
